title: Tokyo Babylon
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In late-bubble-era Tokyo, sixteen-year-old Subaru Sumeragi, head of an onmyoji clan, takes on one supernatural case after another with his twin sister Hokuto and Seishiro, a veterinarian who says he loves him. Many cases are tied to social problems of the city, and the episodic stories grow darker toward a tragic ending.
life_message: Caring for strangers' suffering matters, even in a cold city, though kindness can be betrayed.

content.note: Assassin clan, violent spirits and a graphic act near the end (AnimeUK vol. 5 review; AniList Assassins, Tragedy).
Ghosts, possession and death-centred cases (AnimeUK reviews; AniList Ghost, Exorcism).
Teasing BL romance between 16-year-old Subaru and 25-year-old Seishiro; reviewer flags the age gap; an adult affair in one case.
A karaoke-bar case; nothing else documented.
Case about a family suicide over debt and an elderly man who feels a burden; one review only (to verify).
Hokuto shrugs off environmental rules; framed as a talking point.
Fashion and a haunted designer suit in one case.

dominant: Onmyoji occult; compassion; urban social commentary; tragedy

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Subaru resolves cases through understanding and purification, not retaliation.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Hokuto's rule-shrugging and Subaru's personal choices weigh against clan rules like the gloves.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Clan heirship balanced by help given to any Tokyo stranger.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Grandmother's authority and clan rank; Subaru treats all clients equally.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Ancient onmyoji tradition central, applied to modern urban issues.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Fashion, identity, and tolerance; critique of bubble-era materialism.

folkways.japan: The onmyoji (yin-yang diviner) tradition, clan headship and the 1990 bubble economy are Japanese settings the series draws on.

delivery.evidence: Reviews say cases discuss ozone damage, ageism, organ shortages and housing; MangaUpdates votes Social Commentary.

personified.ideology: compassion for every person and spirit
carefree indifference to rules like environmental ones
the assassin clan's hidden detachment (to verify)

delivery.note: Each case raises a social problem in conversation, but people who do harm are often shown as desperate rather than simply wicked.

winners_losers: Subaru's kindness gets the story's sympathy but is set up for betrayal; desperate people pushed by social pressures are shown with pity.
